BURHAN:v1p100/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p100/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p100/r7.claim: فبشر عباد in al-Zumar is counted as an ending because what follows can be estimated as both an object and a predicate.
BURHAN:v1p100/r7.anchor: ومنها ﴿ فبشر عباد ﴾ بالزمر لتقدير تاليه مفعولا ومبتدأ

DAMGHANI:v1p293/r19.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r19.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r19.claim: Ṭāghūt can mean idols that people worship.
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r19.anchor: الطاغوت الاوثان قوله سبحانه في سورة الزمر

QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r5.claim: Each person's idol is the lower self; one avoids serving it by opposing desire and embracing the Lord's pleasure.
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r5.anchor: طاغوت كل إنسان نفسه ؛ وإنما يجتنب الطاغوت

QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r6.claim: Turning back to God means returning to Him in every matter.
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r6.anchor: أي رجعوا إليه في كل شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verse about avoiding false gods was revealed about Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Salman, and Abu Dharr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد: نزلت والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت في زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وسلمان وأبي ذر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r7.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r7.claim: Ibn Ishaq says it refers to ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, Saʿid ibn Zayd, and al-Zubayr, who embraced Islam after Abu Bakr invited them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: الإشارة بها إلى عبد الرحمن بن عوف، وسعد بن أبي وقاص، وسعيد بن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r8.claim: The occasion reports do not restrict the verse; it remains applicable to people through the end of time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r8.anchor: وهي محكمة في الناس إلى يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan reads the singular ṭāghūt in the plural, ṭawāghīt; “to worship them” is an explicative verbal noun in apposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r9.anchor: والطاغوت: تقدم الكلام عليها في البقرة. وقرأ الحسن: الطواغيت جمعا. أن يعبدوها: أي عبادتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r10.claim: The good news is God's reward; “give good news to My servants” explicitly identifies the people who avoided false worship and turned to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r10.anchor: لهم البشرى: أي من الله تعالى بالثواب. فبشر عباد: هم المجتنبون الطاغوت إلى الله.

DURR-FULL:v7p216/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the verses about avoiding idols were revealed regarding Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Abu Dharr, and Salman, who professed monotheism before Islam.
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r5.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم في قوله {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها} قال: نزلت هاتان الآيتان في ثلاثة نفر

DURR-FULL:v7p216/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r6.claim: Ibn Umar names Saʿid ibn Zayd, Abu Dharr, and Salman as people who followed the best speech in pre-Islamic times, namely the testimony that there is no god but God.
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: كان سعيد بن زيد وأبو ذر وسلمان يتبعون في الجاهلية أحسن القول

THALABI:v8p226/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p226/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p226/r7.claim: The ṭāghūt are idols; avoiding their worship and returning to God means turning back to worship Him, with good news of Paradise in this life and the next.
THALABI:v8p226/r7.anchor: والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت الأوثان أن يعبدوها وأنابوا رجعوا له إلى الله إلى عبادة الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r3.claim: The Taghut they avoid worshipping means idols; those who turn back to God do so through obedience and receive good news of Paradise.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r3.anchor: { والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت } أي: الأوثان { أن يعبدوها وأنابوا إلى الله }

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r6.claim: Believers receive glad tidings; the Prophet's call appeals to people of understanding, and he is not responsible for those whose deeds make them fuel for Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r6.anchor: his call will only appeal to men of understanding; it is not his responsibility to guide those who have become the fuel of Hell

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r1.claim: Al-ṭāghūt comprehensively means anything anti-God: idols and deities, devils and jinn, or leaders who divert people from worship and obedience to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r1.anchor: It is a comprehensive word to denote anything that is anti-God whether idols, deities, devils and jinn

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r2.claim: In contrast with the losers, those who turn from worshipping others and devote themselves sincerely to God receive glad tidings of eternal success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r2.anchor: Here in contrast to the losers whose fate is mentioned earlier, the sincere are mentioned

NAHHAS:v4p7/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r18.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v4p7/r18.anchor: قال الأخفش الطاغوت جمع ويجوز أن يكون واحدة مؤنثة

NAHHAS:v4p7/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p7/r19.claim: Alternatively, الطاغوت may be one feminine singular form.
NAHHAS:v4p7/r19.anchor: الطاغوت جمع ويجوز أن يكون واحدة مؤنثة

SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r1.claim: The feminine pronoun in يعبدوها refers to الطاغوت, treated as feminine; its discussion was given earlier in al-Baqara.
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r1.anchor: الضمير عائد على الطاغوت لأنها تؤنث، وقد تقدم القول عليها مستوفى في البقرة.

SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r2.claim: أن يعبدوها is an accusative بدل اشتمال from الطاغوت, effectively “avoid worship of the ṭāghūt.”
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r2.anchor: في محل نصب على البدل من الطاغوت بدل اشتمال، كأنه قيل: اجتنبوا عبادة الطاغوت.

SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r3.claim: The relative phrase والذين اجتنبوا is the subject.
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r3.anchor: والموصول مبتدأ. والجملة من " لهم البشرى " الخبر.

SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r4.claim: He prefers parsing لهم as predicate and البشرى as its subject; another parse makes the whole clause لهم البشرى the predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r4.anchor: " لهم " هو الخبر بنفسه. " والبشرى " فاعل به وهذا أولى لأنه من باب الإخبار بالمفردات.

SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r5.claim: The explicit noun عبادي replaces a pronoun meaning “them,” referring to those who shunned idolatry and making that description explicit.
SAMIN-DURR:39:17/r5.anchor: " فبشر عبادي " من إيقاع الظاهر موقع المضمر أي: فبشرهم أي: أولئك المجتنبين، وإنما فعل ذلك تصريحا بالوصف المذكور.

ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r1.claim: The ṭāghūt here refers to devils whom the believers avoid following.
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r1.anchor: أي الذين اجتنبوا الشياطين أن يتبعوهم

ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n20/r1.claim: Here taghut refers to seductive evil ambitions such as power-seeking, exploitative wealth, or immoral advancement, which disorient people and enslave them to passion.
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n20/r1.anchor: this term apparently circumscribes the seductive force of certain evil ambitions or desires - like striving after power for its own sake

ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n21/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n21/r1.claim: Asad cross-references the glad tidings to 10:62–64.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr is reported with عبادي and a fatḥa on its yāʾ; ʿUbayd says he pauses at an āya ending and otherwise connects عبادي الذين, calling this the separated reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r1.anchor: قال: قرأ أبو عمرو وحده: فبشر عبادي. الذين [الزمر/ 17، 18] بنصب الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأهل مكة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r2.claim: The al-Qaṭʿī transmission from ʿUbayd and Shibl reports Ibn Kathīr and the people of Mecca with عبادي and fatḥa on the yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r2.anchor: القطعي عن عبيد عن شبل عن ابن كثير وأهل مكة: فبشر عبادي. الذين بنصب الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r3.speaker: قنبل
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r3.claim: Qunbul, from al-Nabbāl and Ibn Kathīr’s associates, reads عباد الذين without yāʾ, with kasra on the dāl.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r3.anchor: وقرأت على قنبل عن النبال عن أصحابه عن ابن كثير: عباد. الذين بكسر الدال من غير ياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r4.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r4.claim: The remaining readers read عباد الذين without a yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: عباد. الذين بغير ياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r5.claim: Al-Fārisī considers both leaving the yāʾ quiescent and vocalizing it acceptable.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r5.anchor: التسكين في الياء حسن، والتحريك فيها أيضا حسن

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads اجتنبوا الطاغوت; the author recalls his earlier account of the word's morphology.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r2.claim: He derives ṭāghūt as a metathesized faʿalūt verbal noun from ṭaghayta: طغيان shows the final radical is yāʾ; the path is طغيوت > طيغوت > طاغوت, while طواغيت reflects the dialect طغوت.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r2.anchor: قد تقدم القول على حديث الطاغوت2 وأنه مقلوب، ووزنه فلعوت من طغيت، وقالوا أيضا: طغوت.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r3.claim: He compares the pattern and plural to forms such as حانوت/حوانيت, deriving حانوت through metathesis and vowel change from حنووت; its relative حانوي is supported by ʿUmāra's poem.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r3.anchor: ومثلها سواء الحانوت، وهي في الأصل حنووت، فعلوت من حنوت؛ لأن الحانوت يحنو على ما فيه،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r4.claim: An alternative derives طواغيت from ṭaghaytu but analogizes its shape to فاعول plurals such as عاقول/عواقيل and ساجور/سواجير; this is acceptable, though the first account is nearer.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p236/r4.anchor: ويجوز في الطواغيت وجه آخر، وهو أن يكون من طغيت، إلا أنه لما قدم اللام وقبلها،

NASHR:v2p363/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p363/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p363/r9.claim: Al-Susi retains the yāʾ in فبشر عبادي when joining, with disagreement about stopping; Yaqub follows his usual rule at pause.
NASHR:v2p363/r9.anchor: فبشر عبادي أثبتها وصلا مفتوحة السوسي

NASHR:v2p163/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p163/r1.speaker: الداني وغيره
NASHR:v2p163/r1.claim: Al-Dānī and others count 212 disputed possessive yāʾs; some count 214 by adding آتاني الله and فبشر عبادي, while others count 216 by adding two more examples.
NASHR:v2p163/r1.anchor: وجملته مائتا ياء واثنتا عشرة ياء، وقد عدها الداني، وغيره

NASHR:v2p163/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p163/r2.speaker: آخرون
NASHR:v2p163/r2.claim: Some authorities reach 216 by additionally counting ألا تتبعن in Ṭā Hā and إن يردن الرحمن in Yā Sīn.
NASHR:v2p163/r2.anchor: وهما ألا تتبعن في طه إن يردن الرحمن في يس فجعلوها مائتين وست عشرة

NASHR:v2p163/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p163/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p163/r3.claim: The author prefers classifying these four examples among the extra yāʾs because the codex omits them, although they also vary between fatḥ and sukūn.
NASHR:v2p163/r3.anchor: وذكر هذه الأربع في باب الزوائد، أولى لحذفها في الرسم وإن كان لها تعلق بهذا الباب

NASHR:v2p193/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p193/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عقيل
NASHR:v2p193/r2.claim: Abu ʿAmr allowed stopping without yāʾ if the phrase counted as an āya, with yāʾ if it did not, and yāʾ when continuing into al-ladhīna.
NASHR:v2p193/r2.anchor: فقال عبيد بن عقيل عن أبي عمرو: إن كانت رأس آية وقفت على عباد وإن لم تكن رأس آية

NASHR:v2p193/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p193/r3.speaker: ابن مجاهد
NASHR:v2p193/r3.claim: Ibn Mujāhid says Abu ʿAmr's book shows he followed the early Medinan verse count; readers using other counts omit the yāʾ, while those using that count retain it.
NASHR:v2p193/r3.anchor: وقال ابن مجاهد: في كتاب أبي عمرو في رواية عباس وابن اليزيدي دليل على أن أبا عمرو

NASHR:v2p193/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p193/r4.speaker: ابن اليزيدي
NASHR:v2p193/r4.claim: Ibn al-Yazīdī views establishing yāʾ in connected recitation and at pause as inconsistent with Abu ʿAmr's stated practice of following the written form at pauses; he thinks Abu ʿAmr overlooked the verse ending.
NASHR:v2p193/r4.anchor: وقال ابن اليزيدي في كتابه في الوصل والقطع: لما ذكر لأبي عمرو الفتح وصلا وإثبات الياء وقفا

NASHR:v2p193/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p193/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v2p193/r5.claim: Al-Dānī says Abu ʿAmr's alternatives show he recognized that this is an āya ending in some counting traditions and applied his usual rules accordingly.
NASHR:v2p193/r5.anchor: وقال الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني بعد ذكره ما قدمنا: قول أبي عمرو لعبيد بن عقيل دليل

NASHR:v2p193/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p193/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p193/r6.claim: Only Mecca and the early Medinan count leave this outside the verse count; Abu ʿAmr followed Hijazi reading and counting first, then Basran counting, consistently following both traditions.
NASHR:v2p193/r6.anchor: والذي لم يعدها آية هو المكي والمدني الأول فقط وعدها غيرهما آية فعلى ما قرروا

QIRAAT-ER:39:17:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:17:16#1/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:39:17:16#1/r1.claim: The ten-reading form explicitly pronounces the final possessive yāʾ, making “My servants” fully audible.
QIRAAT-ER:39:17:16#1/r1.anchor: Yz, mutawatir: The 10-reading pronounces the final yāʾ of the first-person possessive explicitly

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verse was revealed about three men in pre-Islamic times who professed that there is no god but God: Zayd b. ʿAmr b. Nufayl, Salmān, and Abū Dharr.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد : نزلت في ثلاثة نفر كانوا في الجتهلية يقولون لا إله إلا الله زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وسلمان وأبي ذر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq identifies ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf, Saʿd b. Abī Waqqāṣ, Saʿīd b. Zayd, and al-Zubayr: after Abū Bakr became Muslim, they asked him, heard his reminder of God, and all believed; the verse remains applicable through Judgment Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r2.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق : أشير بها إلى عبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد بن أبي وقاص وسعيد بن زيد والزبير

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī derives ṭāghūt as faʿalūt from ṭughyān, rejecting a proposed fāʿūl derivation by metathesis; the unused roots ṭ-w-gh and ṭ-y-gh support his derivation.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r3.anchor: والطاغوت فعلوت من الطغيان كما قالوا لا فاعول كما قيل بتقديم اللام على العين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r4.claim: Its underlying form may be ṭaghiyūt or ṭaghuwūt, from either yāʾ or wāw, since both ṭaghā-yaghā and ṭaghā-yaghū occur in Arabic.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r4.anchor: وأصله طغيوت أو طغووت من الياء أو الواو لأن طغى يطغى ويطغو كلاهما ثابتان في العربية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r5.speaker: الجوهري
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r5.claim: Al-Jawharī records ṭughyān and ṭughwān as synonymous; the plural ṭawāghīt likewise suggests formation on wāw.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r5.anchor: نقله الجوهري ونقل أن الطغيان والطغوان بمعنى وكذا الراغب وجمعه على الطواغيت يدل على أن الجمع بني على الواو

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r6.speaker: الجوهري
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r6.claim: Al-Jawharī defines ṭāghūt as a soothsayer, Satan, or any leader in misguidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r6.anchor: وهو على ما في الصحاح الكاهن والشيطان وكل رأس في الضلال

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r7.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib applies the term to every transgressor and every being worshiped besides God, including sorcerers, soothsayers, rebellious jinn, and those who divert from good; it can be singular or plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r7.anchor: وقال الراغب : هو عبارة عن كل متعد وكل معبود من دون الله تعالى وسمي به الساحر والكاهن والمارد من الجن

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says in this sūra that the term applies only to Satan.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في هذه السورة : لا يطلق على غير الشيطان

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the word's force through the intensive faʿalūt pattern, its conversion from a verbal noun to a name, and metathesis; elsewhere he applies it to Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf for extreme rebellion and hostility to the Messenger, or by comparison to Satan.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r9.anchor: وذكر أن فيه مبالغات من حيث البناء فإن صيغة فعلوت للمبالغة ولذا قالوا الرحموت الرحمة الواسعة ومن حيث التسمية بالمصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r10.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r10.claim: Al-Kashf suggests al-Zamakhsharī means the word is literal only for Satan after its common transfer to him, and metaphorical for others through a visible relation.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r10.anchor: وفي الكشف كأنه لما رآه مصدرا في الأصل منقولا إلى العين كثير الإستعمال في الشيطان حكم بأنه حقيقة فيه بعد النقل مجاز في الباقي

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī thinks ṭāghūt began as a verbal noun for transgression, then named the utmost transgressor; applying the general concept to Satan or another instance can be literal or metaphorical, while Satan dominates usage as chief of transgressors.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r11.anchor: والذي يغلب على الظن أن الطاغوت في الأصل مصدر نقل إلى البالغ الغاية في الطغيان وتجاوز الحد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r12.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r12.claim: Mujāhid identifies the ṭāghūt in this verse as Satan.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r13.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the word as the plural ṭawāghīt, supporting interpretation as devils.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r14.claim: The clause “that they worship them” is a بدل اشتمال from ṭāghūt.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r14.anchor: بدل اشتمال من الطاغوت وعبادة غير الله تعالى عبادة للشيطان

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r15.claim: Worship of anything besides God counts as worship of Satan because Satan commands and embellishes it; the connection is direct if ṭāghūt means idols.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r15.anchor: وعبادة غير الله تعالى عبادة للشيطان إذ هو الآمر بها والمزين لها

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r16.claim: Turning back to God means wholly turning toward Him and away from everything else.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r16.anchor: وأقبلوا إليه سبحانه معرضين عما سواه إقبالا كليا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r17.claim: Their glad tidings are of God's reward, conveyed by messengers or angels at death, at gathering, and afterward.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252/r17.anchor: بالثواب من الله تعالى على ألسنة الرسل عليهم السلام أو الملائكة عند حضور الموت وحين يحشرون وبعد ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r7.claim: The explicit noun replaces a pronoun to honor them, reiterate their entitlement, and show their eagerness to choose obedience and closeness to God; it confirms their turning back and completes the thought.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r7.anchor: ووضع الظاهر موضع الضمير ليشرفهم تعالى بالإضافة إليه ولتكرير بيان الإستحقاق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#3/r1.anchor: ذلك يخوف الله به عباده يا عباد فاتقون} . {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت} الأوثان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#3/r2.claim: They turned back to worshipping God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#3/r2.anchor: وأنابوا إلى الله} رجعوا إلى عبادة الله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#3/r3.claim: They receive good news in this world and Paradise in the next life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#3/r3.anchor: لهم البشرى} في الدنيا والجنة في العقبى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says the two verses concern Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, Abū Dharr, and Salmān, who professed God's oneness before Islam; the best word is lā ilāha illā Allāh.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r8.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: نزلت "والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت" الآيتان،

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r4.claim: Ṭāghūt derives from ṭughyān in an emphatic verbal pattern, then serves as an emphatic epithet used particularly of Satan.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r4.anchor: البالغ غاية الطغيان فعلوت منه بتقديم اللام على العين

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r5.claim: “That they worship it” is an apposition of inclusion to ṭāghūt.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r6.claim: They turn wholly to God, away from everything else.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r7.claim: Their reward is announced by messengers or angels at death.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r7.anchor: بالثواب على ألسنة الرسل، أو الملائكة عند حضور الموت

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r1.claim: Avoiding taghut requires resisting desires that pull people toward it, especially when Satan embellishes it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r1.anchor: كلفوا أنفسهم ذلك لما لها في الانسياق إليه من الهوى مع تزيين الشيطان

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r2.claim: Taghut is anything worshipped besides God; it derives from ṭughyān, is intensive, and rhetorically makes the entity itself an embodiment of transgression.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r2.anchor: وهو كل ما عبد من دون الله , فلغوت من الطغيان وهو صيغة مبالغة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r3.claim: The general command to avoid taghut is specified by بدل اشتمال as avoiding its worship; its feminine designation accompanies believers' divinely aided overcoming of it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r3.anchor: ولما ذكر اجتنابها مطلقا ترغيبا فيه , بين خلاصة ما يجتنب لأجله مع التنفير منها بتأنيثها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r4.claim: Ināba is a complete return to God, turning wholly toward the One whose perfect attributes leave no alternative destination.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r4.anchor: رجعوا رجوعا عظيما أزالوا فيه النوبة وجعلوها إقبالة واحدة لا صرف فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r5.claim: Their glad tidings come through messengers in this life and from angels at death; they profit from God's speech by devoting their religion sincerely to Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r5.anchor: في الدنيا على ألسنة الرسل وعند الموت تتلقاهم الملائكة فقد ربحوا ربحا لا خسارة معه لأنهم انتفعوا بكلام الله فأخلصوا دينهم له

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r6.claim: The shift from an expected “give them glad tidings” to “give glad tidings to My servants” honors them and generalizes the promise by their devotion to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r6.anchor: ولكنه أظهر تعميما وتعليقا بالوصف فقال مسببا عن عملهم , صارفا القول إلى التكلم بالإفراد تشريفا للمبشرين الموصوفين

DURR-FULL:v7p217/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies al-Taghut as Satan and says the singular form here denotes a collective, like singular address to all people as “O human.”
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r2.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال {الطاغوت} الشيطان هو ههنا واحد وهي جماعة

DURR-FULL:v7p217/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت} قال: الشيطان

DURR-FULL:v7p217/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r4.claim: Qatada glosses turning to God as coming back to Him and says the best speech they follow is obedience to God.
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {وأنابوا إلى الله لهم البشرى} قال: أقبلوا إلى الله {فبشر عباد الذين يستمعون

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says these two verses were revealed about three people who professed monotheism in the pre-Islamic period: Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, and Salman al-Farisi.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم في قوله : والذين اجتنبو الطاغوت ان يعبدوها قال : نزلت هاتان الايتان في ثلاثة نفر كانوا في الجاهلية

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the taghut as Satan and explains its singular form as referring collectively to people, as in other singular expressions addressed to humankind.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3249/r2.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال : الطاغوت الشيطان هو ههنا واحد وهي جماعة مثل قوله : يا ايها الانسان ما غرك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r3.claim: The divine possessive ‘servants’ in both occurrences addresses all people, believers and unbelievers, since all fear punishment; its severity ranges up to the polytheists’ everlasting punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r3.anchor: العباد المضاف إلى ضمير الجلالة في الموضعين هنا يعم كل عبد من الناس من مؤمن وكافر إذ الجميع يخافون العذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r5.claim: The command to fear God follows the threat because warning implies punishment is prepared for the disobedient, making taqwā the fitting next instruction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r5.anchor: فناسب أن يعقب بأمر الناس بالتقوى للتفادي من العذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r6.claim: The vocative precedes the consequent command to focus attention in this warning context; in 2:197, pilgrimage exhortation instead places the command before the vocative and joins it with wāw.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r6.anchor: لأن المقام هنا مقام تحذير وترهيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r7.claim: The yāʾ of the first-person suffix is deleted in ‘yā ʿibād’ according to one of five possible forms for a vocative annexed to that suffix.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r7.anchor: على أحد وجوه خمسة في المنادى المضاف إلى ياء المتكلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r8.claim: After threatening polytheists and admonishing everyone, the discourse turns to believers’ good news, in contrast to the warning; the clause signals why they merit it and answers 39:16.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p362#2/r8.anchor: لما انتهى تهديد المشركين وموعظة الخلائق أجمعين ثني عنان الخطاب إلى جانب المؤمنين فيما يختص بهم من البشارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r1.claim: The author analyzes ṭāghūt as a verbal or deverbal noun from ṭaghā on the pattern faʿalūt, like raḥamūt and malakūt; the root’s final weak letter has both wāw and yāʾ forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r1.anchor: والطاغوت : مصدر أو اسم مصدر طغا على وزن فعلوت بتحريك العين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r2.speaker: القاموس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r2.claim: Al-Qāmūs appears to favor a wāw in the root form; the following pattern-wāw makes the final weak letter heavy, prompting metathesis and the form ṭāghūt, with tāʾ added for intensification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r2.anchor: وإذ كانت لامه حرف علة ووقعت بعدها واو زنة فعلوت استثقلت الضمة عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r3.speaker: من العلماء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r3.claim: Some scholars treat ṭāghūt as a foreign word on the pattern fāʿūl; al-Itqān says it means ‘soothsayer’ in Abyssinian, and Ibn Ḥajar added it to Ibn al-Subkī’s list of Quranic loanwords.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r3.anchor: وذكره في ( الإتقان ) فيما وقع في القرآن من المعرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r4.claim: In Quran and Sunna, ṭāghūt denotes a powerful force in unbelief or oppression: an idol, a group of idols, or a leader of unbelievers such as Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf; here it means idols collectively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r4.anchor: وأطلق الطاغوت في القرآن والسنة على القوي في الكفر أو الظلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r5.claim: The plural ṭawāghīt reflects predominance of its nominal use, though a single idol is an uncommon referent; feminine ‘worship them’ treats it as a nonrational plural.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r5.anchor: وأما جمعه على طواغيت فذلك على تغليب الاسمية علما بالغلبة إذ جعل الطاغوت لواحد الأصنام وهو قليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r6.claim: The feminine pronoun for ṭāghūt agrees with its sense as a nonrational plural; 2:257 uses masculine agreement because it is predicated of masculine plural ‘allies’ or treated as rational by its worshippers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r6.anchor: وباعتبار تنزيلها منزلة العقلاء في زعم عبادها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r7.claim: The clause ‘that they worship them’ is a بدل اشتمال (inclusive apposition) of ṭāghūt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r7.anchor: و { أن يعبدوها } بدل من { الطاغوت } بدل اشتمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r8.claim: Ināba means repentance, as at 11:75; here it means repenting from every sin, above all from the pre-Islamic shirk they practiced.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p364/r8.anchor: والمراد بها هنا التوبة من كل ذنب ومعصية وأعلاها التوبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r1.claim: Bushrā means good news; here it is the good news of Paradise, as in the phrase about good news in this life and the next at 10:64.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r2.claim: Preposing ‘for them’ in ‘for them is the good news’ conveys restriction, paralleling the restrictive clauses in 39:18.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r3.claim: The good-news command refers to those who avoided ṭāghūt; replacing ‘announce to them’ with ‘announce to My servants’ and a relative clause adds praise for devotion to God and hearing and following the best speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r3.anchor: إلى الإظهار باسم العباد مضاف إلى ضمير الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r4.speaker: العشرة ما عدا السوسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r4.claim: All ten readers except al-Sūsī read ʿibādi with kasra on dāl and no yāʾ, a lightening that relies on the kasra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r4.anchor: وقرأ العشرة ما عدا السوسي راوي أبي عمرو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r5.speaker: السوسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r5.claim: Al-Sūsī reads a yāʾ after dāl, open in connected reading and silent at pause; deletion at pause is also reported and both forms are grammatical, though the codices omit the yāʾ, weakening the reading unless treated as performance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r5.anchor: وقرأها السوسي بياء بعد الدال مفتوحة في الوصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verses were revealed about Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Abū Dharr, and Salmān, who avoided idol worship in pre-Islamic times and followed the best teaching that reached them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r7.anchor: وعن ابن زيد نزلت في زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وأبي ذر الغفاري وسلمان الفارسي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the good-news passage was revealed about ʿUthmān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, Saʿīd ibn Zayd, and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who came to Abū Bakr after his conversion, heard his testimony, and believed.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya notes variant readings of ʿibād and says a comparable variation has been discussed earlier.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r5.anchor: واختلفت القراءة في قوله: «عباد» وقد تقدم نظيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the occasion was Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, Salmān al-Fārisī, and Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī, to whom the verse points.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد: إن سبب نزولها زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وسلمان الفارسي وأبو ذر الغفاري، والإشارة إليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r7.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r7.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the verse refers to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Saʿīd ibn Zayd, and al-Zubayr: after Abū Bakr converted, they asked him about it, heard his reminder of God, and all believed, whereupon the verse was revealed about them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r7.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: الإشارة بها إلى عبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد بن أبي وقاص وسعيد بن زيد والزبير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r8.claim: Whatever its reported occasion, the verse applies generally to people through the Day of Resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r8.anchor: وهي على كل حال عامة في الناس إلى يوم القيامة يتناولهم حكمها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r9.claim: Ṭāghūt means anything worshipped besides God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r9.anchor: والطاغوت: كل ما يعبد من دون الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r10.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r10.claim: Mujāhid, al-Suddī, and Ibn Zayd interpret ṭāghūt here as Satan, or as the group of satans; this collective referent explains the feminine pronoun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r10.anchor: والطاغوت أيضا: الشيطان، وبه فسر هنا مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد، وأوقعه هنا على جماعة الشياطين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r11.claim: The feminine pronoun is used because ṭāghūt refers here to a group of satans.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r11.anchor: وأوقعه هنا على جماعة الشياطين، ولذلك أنث الضمير بعد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r1.speaker: ابن زيد عن أبيه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd reports from his father that this verse and the next concerned three pre-Islamic monotheists: Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Abū Dharr, and Salmān al-Fārisī, whom God guided without scripture or prophet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r1.anchor: روى ابن زيد عن أبيه أن هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the ṭāghūt as devils.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r3.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sāʾib identifies the ṭāghūt as soothsayers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r4.claim: Muqātil identifies the ṭāghūt as idols.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r5.claim: On Muqātil’s view that ṭāghūt means idols, the feminine object suffix reflects the feminine referent.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r5.anchor: فعلى قول مقاتل هذا إنما قال يعبدوها لأنها مؤنثة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r6.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the feminine suffix because ṭāghūt can mean a group, or can be treated as one feminine noun.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r6.anchor: وقال الأخفش إنما قال يعبدوها لأن الطاغوت في معنى جماعة وإن شئت جعلته واحدا مؤنثا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r7.claim: They turned back to God through obedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وأنابوا إلى الله ﴾ أي رجعوا إليه بالطاعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r8.claim: The good news promised to them is Paradise.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the bāʾ with kasra and gives the final yāʾ its vowel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p170/r9.anchor: فبشر عبادي / بباء وحرك الياء أبو عمرو

BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r3.claim: Ijtinab means moving aside and keeping away.
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r3.anchor: الاجتناب : بايك سو شدن). يقال : اجتنب

BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r4.claim: Taghut denotes the utmost degree of rebellion, exceeding the limit in disobedience; its form is an intensive derivative of tugyan.
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r4.anchor: والطاغوت : البالغ أقصى غاية الظغيان ، وهو تجاوز الحد في العصيان ، فلعوت من الطغيان

BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r5.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r5.claim: Kashf al-Asrar treats ta as an added intensifier, not a feminine ending, like forms such as malakut and jabarut.
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r5.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : التاء ليست بأصلية ، هي في الطاغوت كهي في الملكوت والجبروت

BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r6.speaker: الكواشي والمفردات والقاموس
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r6.claim: The term is used in masculine and feminine forms and can refer to one or many.
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r6.anchor: ويذكر ؛ أي : الطاغوت ويؤنث كما في "الكواشي" ، ويستعمل في الواحد والجمع كما في "المفردات" و"القاموس"

BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r7.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r7.claim: Al-Raghib defines taghut as any transgressor and anything worshipped besides God.
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r7.anchor: قال الراغب : وهو عبارة عن كل متعد وكل معبود من دون الله.

BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r8.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r8.claim: Al-Qamus lists al-Lat, al-Uzza, soothsayers, Satan, leaders of misguidance, idols, anything worshipped besides God, and rebellious People of the Book.
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r8.anchor: وفي "القاموس" : الطاغوت اللات والعزى والكاهن والشيطان وكل رأس ضلال والأصنام وكل ما عبد من دون الله

BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r9.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r9.claim: Kashf al-Asrar says anyone who worships another thing is a rebel, and the object worshipped is taghut.
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r9.anchor: وقال في "كشف الأسرار" : كل من عبد شيئا غير الله ، فهو طاغغ ومعبوده : طاغوت.

BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r10.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r10.claim: Al-Tawilat al-Najmiyya identifies each person's taghut with the self; avoidance means opposing desire, embracing God's pleasure, and returning wholly to Him by leaving all else.
BURSEVI:v8p66#2/r10.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : طاغوت كل أحد نفسه وإنما يجتنب الطاغوت من خالف هواه وعانق رضا مولاه

BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r1.speaker: سهل
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r1.claim: Sahl identifies taghut with the world: its root is ignorance, branches food and drink, adornment boasting, fruit sins, and inheritance hardness and punishment.
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r1.anchor: وقال سهل : الطاغوت : الدنيا وأصلها الجهل وفرعها المآكل والمشارب وزينتها التفاخر وثمرتها المعاصي

BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r2.claim: The phrase that they worship it is a substitution of inclusion from taghut.
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r2.anchor: {أن يعبدوها} بدل اشتمال منه ، فإن عبادة غير الله عبادة للشيطان

BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r3.claim: Worshipping anything besides God counts as Satan worship because Satan commands and beautifies it.
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r3.anchor: فإن عبادة غير الله عبادة للشيطان إذ هو الآمر بها والمزين لها.

BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r4.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r4.claim: Bahr al-Ulum says taghut here is intended collectively, as a plural.
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r4.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : وفيها إشارة إلى أن المراد بالطاغوت ها هنا الجمع.

BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r5.claim: Turning to God means approaching Him completely while turning away from everything besides Him.
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r5.anchor: {وأنابوا إلى الله} وأقبلوا عليه معرضين عما سواه إقبالا كليا.

BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r6.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r6.claim: Al-Bahr explains shunning taghut as disbelief in it and turning to God as belief in Him, as in the verse about grasping the firmest handhold.
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r6.anchor: قال في "البحر" : واعلم أن المراد باجتناب الطاغوت الكفر بها وبالإنابة إلى الله الإيمان بالله

BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r7.claim: Shunning taghut precedes turning to God, as disbelief precedes belief and the negation in the testimony of unity precedes affirmation.
BURSEVI:v8p66#3/r7.anchor: وقدم اجتناب الطاغوت على الإنابة إلى الله كما قدم الكفر بالطاغوت على الإيمان بالله

BURSEVI:v8p67/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p67/r1.claim: The good news is reward and the greatest divine approval, conveyed by messengers through revelation in this life or by angels at death, resurrection, and thereafter.
BURSEVI:v8p67/r1.anchor: على ألسنة الرسل بالوحي في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v8p67/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67/r2.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v8p67/r2.claim: Some spiritual masters say the good news is that they belong to the people of divine guidance and grace, the greatest honor.
BURSEVI:v8p67/r2.anchor: وقال بعض الكبار : لهم البشرى بأنهم من أهل الهداية والفضل من الله ، وهي الكرامة الكبرى.

BURSEVI:v8p67/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p67/r3.claim: The Messenger gives glad tidings in this world; angels give them in the afterlife, which follows from the worldly good news.
BURSEVI:v8p67/r3.anchor: تبشير من لسان الرسول عليه السلام ، وهو تبشير في الدنيا.

BURSEVI:v8p67/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p67/r4.claim: The underlying form is ibadi, with the ya deleted.

BURSEVI:v8p67/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67/r7.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v8p67/r7.claim: Al-Irshad says the explicit noun replacing their pronoun honors them and shows their distinction comes from discerning truth from falsehood and choosing the best.
BURSEVI:v8p67/r7.anchor: وقال في "الإرشاد" ونحوه ؛ أي : فبشر ، فوضع الظاهر موضع ضميرهم تشريفا لهم بالإضافة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r1.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, quoting his father, says the verse was revealed about Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Abu Dharr, and Salman al-Farisi.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r1.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه: {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها} نزلت في زيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r2.claim: The correct reading is general: it includes those named and everyone who avoids idol worship and turns to worshiping the Merciful; they receive good news in this life and the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r2.anchor: والصحيح أنها شاملة لهم ولغيرهم، ممن اجتنب عبادة الأوثان، وأناب إلى عبادة الرحمن. فهؤلاء هم الذين لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r1.claim: Abū Muslim derives ṭāghūt from ṭughyān, transgression.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r1.anchor: الطاغوت: فاعول من الطغيان، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r2.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r2.claim: Another view treats ṭāghūt as a foreign name, like Jālūt and Hārūt.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو اسم أعجمي، نحو: جالوت وهاروت.

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r3.claim: A further view assigns ṭāghūt the pattern faʿalūt.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r3.anchor: وقيل: وزنه فعلوت، وقال أبو حاتم

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r4.claim: Abū Ḥātim says Arabs use ṭāghūt as singular or plural and as masculine or feminine.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: والعرب تجعل الطاغوت واحدا وجمعا ومذكرا ومؤنثا

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r5.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī says ṭāghūt comes from ṭaghā with an added tāʾ, which Arabs sometimes add.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r5.anchor: وقيل: أصله طغى زيدت التاء فيه، والعرب تزيد التاء، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r6.claim: Ṭāghūt can mean anything worshipped besides God.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو اسم لكل ما يعبد من دون الله.

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r7.claim: Ināba means return; it is akin to repentance and opposite to persistence.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r7.anchor: والإنابة: الرجوع، ونظيرها: التوبة، ونقيضها: الإصرار.

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r8.claim: Bushrā is news of joy that appears on a person's face.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r8.anchor: والبشرى: الإعلام بما يظهر في بشرة وجهه من السرور.

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r16.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r16.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verse was revealed about three pre-Islamic men who professed that there is no god but God: Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Abū Dharr, and Salmān al-Fārisī.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r16.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: (والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت) الآية: نزلت في ثلاثة نفر

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r17.claim: The promise to the God-fearing follows the warning to disbelievers and sinners, continuing God's practice of joining promise with warning.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r17.anchor: لما تقدم الوعيد للكفار والعصاة عقبه بالوعد للمتقين على عادته تعالى في الجمع بين الوعد والوعيد

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r18.claim: Those described have kept far away from worshipping ṭāghūt.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r18.anchor: فقال سبحانه: والذين اجتنبوا أي: تباعدوا عن الطاغوت أن يعبدوها

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r19.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r19.claim: Mujāhid, al-Suddī, and Ibn Zayd identify ṭāghūt here as idols or Satan.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r19.anchor: قيل: الطاغوت: الأوثان، وقيل: الشيطان، عن مجاهد، والسدي، وابن زيد.

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r20.claim: The feminine pronoun matches the feminine form of ṭāghūt.

JISHUMI:v8p6049/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r21.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r21.claim: Alternatively, ṭāghūt is anything that calls people to worship someone besides God; its feminine form denotes a collective.
JISHUMI:v8p6049/r21.anchor: وقيل: هو كل ما دعا إلى عبادة غير الله، وتأنيثه للجماعة.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r1.claim: Al-ṭāghūt is formed from ṭughyān with the lām moved before the ʿayn, like malakūt and raḥamūt.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r2.claim: The term denotes Satan or devils; its verbal noun form intensifies the sense, naming Satan as sheer transgression, and its restricted use marks the referent.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r3.claim: A variant has the plural al-ṭawāghīt, and the intended referent here is plural.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r3.anchor: قرىء : ( الطواغيت ) { أن يعبدوها } بدل من الطاغوت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r4.claim: The clause that they worship it is an appositive of inclusion explaining al-ṭāghūt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r4.anchor: { أن يعبدوها } بدل من الطاغوت بدل الاشتمال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r5.claim: The glad tidings are reward, conveyed in revelation by the messengers and by angels at death and resurrection; compare 10:64 and 57:12.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r6.claim: My servants means those who shunned idolatry and turned to God; the overt noun replaces a pronoun to specify that they must possess the following quality.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r6.anchor: وإنما أراد بهم أن يكونوا مع الاجتناب والإنابة على هذه الصفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r14.claim: Some stop after give good news to My servants and begin those who listen as a nominative subject, with those are as its predicate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r14.anchor: ومن الوقفة من يقف على : فبشر عبادي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r1.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd identify al-taghut as Satan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن الطاغوت الشيطان , قاله مجاهد وابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi identify it as idols.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r3.claim: One view treats taghut as a foreign name like Harut and Marut.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما : أنه اسم أعجمي مثل هاروت وماروت

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r5.claim: Qatada says it means turning toward God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما : أقبلوا إلى الله , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says it means remaining upright toward God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r6.anchor: الثاني : استقاموا إلى الله , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r7.claim: A further possibility is turning back to God from sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r7.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : وأنابوا إلى الله من ذنوبهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل ويحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r8.claim: Muqatil and Yahya ibn Sallam say the glad tidings are Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r8.anchor: أحدهما : أنها الجنة , قاله مقاتل ويحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r9.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r9.claim: Al-Kalbi says the angels give believers good tidings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r9.anchor: الثاني : بشرى الملائكة للمؤمنين , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r10.claim: Another possibility is good news at death about the reward seen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r10.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : أنها البشرى عند المعاينة بما يشاهده من ثواب عمله

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r19.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r19.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says it concerns Zayd ibn Amr, Abu Dharr, and Salman, who avoided idolatry before Islam and followed reason's best.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r19.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد : نزلت في زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وأبي ذر الغفاري وسلمان الفارسي

MUJAHID:v2p557/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p557/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p557/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the ṭāghūt that they avoid worshipping as Satan.
MUJAHID:v2p557/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها ﴾ يعني الشيطان

MUQATIL:39:17-18/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r1.claim: The taghut here are idols; Muqatil notes that the word is feminine.
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r1.anchor: الذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت } يعنى الأوثان، وهى مؤنثة

MUQATIL:39:17-18/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r2.claim: They turned from worshipping idols back to worshipping God.
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r2.anchor: ورجعوا من عبادة الأوثان إلى عبادة الله عز وجل

MUQATIL:39:17-18/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r3.claim: The glad tidings are of Paradise, and the servants are to be told this good news.
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r3.anchor: لهم البشرى } يعنى الجنة { فبشر عباد } [آية: 17] فبشر عبادى بالجنة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r1.claim: Al-ṭāghūt here means Satan or Satans: it is a verbal noun from ṭughyān, formed with metathesis, and used of Satan as an intensified source-word; its collective sense is plural.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r1.anchor: الشياطين فعلوت من الطغيان كالملكوت والرحموت الا أن فيها قلبا بتقديم اللام على العين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r2.claim: The pattern conveys intensification, as rahamūt is abundant mercy and malakūt expansive dominion; the metathesis makes the form specific to Satan.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r2.anchor: وفيها مبالغات وهى التسمية بالمصدر كأن عين الشيطان طغيان وأن البناء بناء مبالغة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r3.speaker: قُرِئَ
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r3.claim: A variant reading has al-ṭawāghīt, the plural form.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r4.claim: The clause is a بدل اشتمال of al-ṭāghūt, meaning their worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r4.anchor: بدل الاشتمال من الطاغوت أي عبادتها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r5.claim: Anābū means that they returned to God.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r5.anchor: رجعوا ﴿ إلى الله لهم البشرى ﴾ هى البشارة بالثواب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r6.claim: Their glad tidings are reward, received from the angels at death and again when they are gathered.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#7/r6.anchor: هى البشارة بالثواب تتلقاهم الملائكة عند حضور الموت مبشرين وحين يحشرون

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r1.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash says ṭāghūt may be a plural, or a single feminine noun, explaining the feminine pronoun.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش: الطاغوت جمع ويجوز أن تكون واحدة مؤنثة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r2.claim: To avoid the ṭāghūt is to keep away from it and remain apart from it, so as not to worship it.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r2.anchor: أي تباعدوا من الطاغوت وكانوا منها على جانب فلم يعبدوها

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r3.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r3.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd identify the ṭāghūt as Satan.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد وابن زيد: هو الشيطان

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r4.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi identify the ṭāghūt as idols.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r5.claim: Another view identifies the ṭāghūt as a soothsayer.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r6.claim: One view treats ṭāghūt as a foreign name, like Talut, Jalut, Harut, and Marut.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r6.anchor: إنه اسم أعجمي مثل طالوت وجالوت

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r7.claim: Another view derives the Arabic word from ṭughyān, transgression.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r8.claim: The particle an is accusative as a substitute for ṭāghūt, meaning “avoid worshipping the ṭāghūt.”
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r8.anchor: و«أن» في موضع نصب بدلا من الطاغوت، تقديره

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r9.claim: They turned back to worshipping and obeying God.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r10.claim: Their glad tidings are of Paradise in the afterlife, given to them in this life.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r10.anchor: في الحياة الدنيا بالجنة في العقبى

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r11.claim: One reported occasion says the passage concerned Uthman, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Saʿd, Saʿid, Talha, and al-Zubayr: they asked Abu Bakr about faith, heard his account, and believed.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r11.anchor: روي أنها نزلت في عثمان وعبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد وسعيد وطلحة والزبير

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r12.claim: Another view says it concerned Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Abu Dharr, and others who professed God’s oneness before Muhammad’s mission.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r12.anchor: في زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وأبي ذر وغيرهما ممن وحد الله تعالى

QASHANI:39:17-21/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:17-21/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:17-21/r1.claim: Avoiding worship of anything besides God and turning to Him means pure monotheism, whose glad tidings are the encounter with God.
QASHANI:39:17-21/r1.anchor: عبادة الغير { وأنابوا إلى الله } بالتوحيد المحض

QASHANI:39:17-21/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:17-21/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:17-21/r2.claim: The servants to be given glad tidings are those singled out by God's special care.

RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r1.claim: After threatening idol worshippers, God promises those who avoid worshipping idols and shirk; pairing promise with threat throughout gives full encouragement and warning.
RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r1.anchor: من اجتنب عبادتها واحترز عن الشرك

RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r2.claim: The Kashshaf author derives ṭāghūt from ṭughyān on the pattern faʿalūt, with metathesis that puts the root's lām before its ʿayn.
RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r2.anchor: الطاغوت فعلوت من الطغيات كالملكوت والرحموت

RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r3.claim: Al-Razi lists emphatic force in treating the verbal noun as the thing itself, using an intensive pattern (as in vast mercy and expansive dominion), and reversing the root letters.
RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r3.anchor: في هذا اللفظ أنواع من المبالغة أحدها

RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p225/r4.claim: Putting the root's lām before its ʿayn is an unusual word formation chosen only for emphasis.

RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r1.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r1.claim: Some identify taghut as Satan; since Satan prompts idol worship, worshipping idols counts as serving Satan.
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r1.anchor: فقيل إنه الشيطان فإن قيل إنهم ما عبدوا الشيطان وإنما عبدوا الصنم

RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r2.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r2.claim: Others call idols taghuts metaphorically: worshipers transgress, but idols are named for the transgression their sight and proximity cause.
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد بالطاغوت الصنم وسميت طواغيت على سبيل المجاز لأنه لا فعل لها

RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r3.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r3.claim: A further view defines taghut as anything worshipped or obeyed apart from God.
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r3.anchor: وقيل كل ما يعبد ويطاع من دون الله فهو طاغوت

RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r4.speaker: في التواريخ
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r4.claim: Historical accounts say idol worship began with anthropomorphists imagining God as a great light and angels as lights of differing sizes, then worshipping images made to match them.
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r4.anchor: ويقال في التواريخ إن الأصل في عبادة الأصنام ، أن القوم

RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r5.claim: Razi sums up avoiding taghut as turning from servitude to everything besides God, and inaba as returning wholly to worship of God.
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r5.anchor: أي أعرضوا عن عبودية كل ما سوى الله

RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r6.claim: Citing a Torah instruction to answer God with the whole heart, Razi says exclusive devotion does not mean denying created causes; God alone is necessary, while all else is contingent and depends on His bringing it into being.
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r6.anchor: يا موسى أجب إلهك بكل قلبك

RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r7.claim: God arranges some events through intermediaries and others without them; all things are from God, and He alone is the ultimate manager and effective agent.
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r7.anchor: جعل تكوينه للأشياء على قسمين منها ما يكون بغير واسطة

RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r8.claim: Razi recounts advising a young man to protect his reputation and wealth; the youth invoked reliance on decree, but Razi said he had misunderstood a true principle.
RAZI-FULL:v26p225#2/r8.anchor: وقد اتفق أني كنت أنصح بعض الصبيان في حفظ العرض والمال فعارضني وقالا يجوز الاعتماد على الجد والجهد

RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r1.claim: For events in this lower world, God has appointed known causes; the higher world has events without intermediaries.

RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r2.claim: Seeking lower-world outcomes without the means God assigned opposes His wisdom and ordering; reliance on God is compatible with using those means.
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r2.anchor: من طلب حوادث هذا العالم الأسفل لا من الأسباب التي عينها الله تعالى كان هذا الشخص منازعا لله في حكمته

RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r3.claim: The promised glad tidings come near death, in the grave, at the gathering, at the division of the saved and damned, and upon believers' entry into Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r3.anchor: إنها تحصل عند القرب من الموت وعند الوضع في القبر

RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r4.claim: The tidings remove fear of future judgment and grief over lost worldly good, then announce Paradise and its delights and lasting fulfillment.
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r4.anchor: والخوف إنما يكون من المستقبل والحزن إنما يكون بسبب الأحوال الماضية

RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r5.claim: Angels may give the glad tidings at death and on entering Paradise; God may also give them when the believers meet Him.
RAZI-FULL:v26p226/r5.anchor: فنقول يحتمل أن يكون هم الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r1.claim: The fronted phrase implies exclusivity: this glad tidings belongs to those who avoid worship of anything besides God and turn wholly to Him.

RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r2.claim: The definite article in al-bushra suggests the entire kind of glad tidings belongs to them, leaving no share for others.
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r2.anchor: أن الألف واللام في لفظ البشرى مفيد للماهية

RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r3.claim: Since glad tidings are the first announcement of good, rewards already known in worldly life would merely repeat old news; the tidings therefore promise further bliss, including what no soul knows.
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r3.anchor: فثبت أن هذه البشارة لا تتحقق إلا إذا حصل الإخبار بحصول أنواع أخر من السعادات فوق ما عرفوها وسمعوها في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r4.claim: Because God Himself announces the reward after such a demanding condition, its greatness exceeds what minds can fully describe.
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r4.anchor: هو الله تعالى وهو أعظم العظماء

STUDYQURAN:39:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:17/r1.claim: Al-ṭāghūt denotes false authorities, objects of worship, and causes; shunning such sources concerns rejecting worship of whatever is other than God.
STUDYQURAN:39:17/r1.anchor: False deities translates al-ṭāghūt, which denotes a variety of false sources of authority, false objects of worship, and false causes

STUDYQURAN:39:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:17/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:39:17/r2.claim: Ṭ says shunning false deities entails avoiding worship of everything other than God.
STUDYQURAN:39:17/r2.anchor: shunning the worship of all that is other than God (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:39:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:17/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:39:17/r3.claim: Ṭ reports that some take al-ṭāghūt as singular and identify it with Satan.
STUDYQURAN:39:17/r3.anchor: Some take al-ṭāghūt to be singular and thus understand it to mean Satan (Ṭ)

TAB-FULL:v20p183/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r1.claim: Those praised avoided worship of anything worshipped besides God; al-Ṭabarī says the taghut has the same meaning here as elsewhere.
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r1.anchor: بمعنى واحد عندنا ذكر من قال ما ذكرنا في هذا الموضع

TAB-FULL:v20p183/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the taghut as Satan.
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت} [الزمر: 17] قال: «الشيطان»

TAB-FULL:v20p183/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r3.claim: Al-Suddī also identifies the taghut as Satan.
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r3.anchor: السدي {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها} [الزمر: 17] قال: «الشيطان»

TAB-FULL:v20p183/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the taghut here as Satan and describes the referent as one while its expression carries a collective sense.
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r4.anchor: ابن زيد، في قوله: {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها} [الزمر: 17] قال: «الشيطان هو هاهنا واحد وهي جماعة»

TAB-FULL:v20p183/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r5.claim: The feminine pronoun is used because taghut is treated as feminine and, in this explanation, as a collective.
TAB-FULL:v20p183/r5.anchor: ابن زيد، في قوله: {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها} [الزمر: 17] قال: «الشيطان هو هاهنا واحد وهي جماعة»

TAB-FULL:v20p184/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p184/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p184/r1.claim: They repent and return to affirming God's oneness, obeying Him, and dissociating themselves from other gods and idols.
TAB-FULL:v20p184/r1.anchor: قتادة، قوله: {وأنابوا إلى الله} [الزمر: 17] : «وأقبلوا إلى الله»

TAB-FULL:v20p184/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p184/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p184/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses turning back to God as turning toward Him.
TAB-FULL:v20p184/r2.anchor: قتادة، قوله: {وأنابوا إلى الله} [الزمر: 17] : «وأقبلوا إلى الله»

TAB-FULL:v20p184/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p184/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p184/r3.claim: Al-Suddī glosses it as responding to God.
TAB-FULL:v20p184/r3.anchor: السدي، قوله: {وأنابوا إلى الله} [الزمر: 17] قال: «أجابوا إليه»

TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r1.claim: Their glad tidings in this world are Paradise in the next; al-Ṭabarī also says they leave speech without sound guidance.
TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r1.anchor: ويتركون ما سوى ذلك من القول الذي لا يدل على رشاد، ولا يهدي إلى سداد وبنحو الذي قلنا

TAB-FULL:v20p185/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p185/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p185/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd reports from his father that these verses concerned Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Abū Dharr, and Salmān, who professed God's oneness and rejected idols before Islam, without a book or prophet.
TAB-FULL:v20p185/r2.anchor: ابن زيد، في قوله: {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها. . .} [الزمر: 17] الآيتين " حدثني أبي أن هاتين الآيتين نزلتا في ثلاثة نفر

SULAMI:v2p194#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p194#4/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p194#4/r1.claim: Sahl identifies the taghut with this world: ignorance is its root, food and drink its branches, boastfulness its adornment, sins its fruit, and hardness and punishment its inheritance.
SULAMI:v2p194#4/r1.anchor: قال سهل - رحمة الله عليه - : الطاغوت الدنيا واصلها الجهل وفرعها المأكل والمشرب

TUSTARI:39:17/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:39:17/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:39:17/r1.claim: The false deity avoided here is worldly life: ignorance is its root, food and drink its branches, boasting its adornment, sins its fruit, and hardness and punishment its measure.
TUSTARI:39:17/r1.anchor: الطاغوت الدنيا، وأصلها الجهل، وفرعها المآكل والمشارب

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib defines ṭāghūt as every transgressor and every object worshipped apart from God, and says the term is used for singular and plural.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r3.anchor: قال الراغب الطاغوت عبارة عن كل متعد وكل معبود من دون الله

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r4.claim: The verse most likely means idols and every false deity worshipped apart from God.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بها في الآية الأوثان وكل معبود طاغ من دون الله

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r5.claim: Avoiding false worship alone is insufficient; what benefits people is both negation and affirmation: worshipping God alone and sincerely leaving every other object of worship.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى أن مجرد النفي لا يجدي شيئا بل الذي ينفع الإنسان مجموع النفي والإثبات

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r6.claim: The phrase announces glad tidings and serves as the predicate about those who avoid the false deities and turn to God.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r6.anchor: قوله { لهم البشرى } إنشاء بشرى وخبر لقوله { والذين اجتنبوا } الخ

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r7.claim: The wording could have said give them glad tidings; calling them My servants honors them, then characterizes them as people who listen to speech and follow its best.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r7.anchor: فبشر عباد واضيف إلى ضمير التكلم لتشريفهم به

TABRISI:39:17-19/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19/r3.claim: The clause is an accusative substitute for al-ṭāghūt, meaning ‘avoided worshipping it.’
TABRISI:39:17-19/r3.anchor: { أن يعبدوها } في موضع نصب بدل من الطاغوت والتقدير والذين اجتنبوا عبادة الطاغوت

TABRISI:39:17-19/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19/r4.claim: ‘For them is good news’ predicates ‘those who avoided’; al-bushrā is raised through the adverbial functioning as predicate.
TABRISI:39:17-19/r4.anchor: وخبر الذين اجتنبوا قوله { لهم البشرى } والبشرى ترتفع بالظرف لجريه خبرا على المبتدأ

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r1.claim: Al-ṭāghūt refers to idols and Satan.

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r2.claim: Another view includes anyone who calls people to worship something other than God.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: كل من دعا إلى عبادة غير الله تعالى

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r3.claim: The feminine pronoun is used because al-ṭāghūt is a collective.

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r5.claim: They avoided worshipping the false deity.

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r6.claim: They repented and abandoned their former conduct.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r6.anchor: أي تابوا إليه فأقلعوا عما كانوا عليه

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r7.claim: Bushrā is glad tidings that make joy appear on faces, recompense for their conduct.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r7.anchor: أي البشارة وهي الإعلام بما يظهر به السرور في بشرة وجوههم جزاء على ذلك

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r8.speaker: أبو بصير عن أبي عبد الله
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r8.claim: Abū Baṣīr reports from Abū ʿAbd Allāh: ‘You are they’; whoever obeys a tyrant has worshipped him.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r8.anchor: وروى أبو بصير عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: أنتم هم ومن أطاع جبارا فقد عبده

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r9.claim: The kasra stands in place of the omitted yāʾ in ‘My servants.’
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r9.anchor: { فبشر } يا محمد { عباد } اجتزأ بالكسرة عن الياء

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r17.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r17.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says the verses came down about three pre-Islamic monotheists: Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, Abū Dharr, and Salmān al-Fārisī.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r17.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: نزل قوله { والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت } الآيتين في ثلاثة نفر

THALABI:v8p227/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p227/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v8p227/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd reports that these two verses concerned Zayd ibn Amr, Abu Dharr, and Salman al-Farisi, three pre-Islamic men who professed that there is no god but God.
THALABI:v8p227/r4.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله: والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت الآيتين: حدثني أبي: أن هاتين الآيتين نزلتا في ثلاثة نفر كانوا في الجاهلية يقولون: لا إله إلا الله، وهم زيد بن عمرو

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r1.claim: Tāghūt covers false deities worshipped by people, visible or invisible beings that prompt disobedience, and efforts to make truth appear false or falsehood true, including unbelief and irreligion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r1.anchor: tâgūt kelimesi insanlar tarafından tapılan bâtıl tanrıları; Allah Teâlâ’ya isyan edilmesine sebep olan, görünür ve görünmez varlıkları; insanlık tarihi boyunca hakkı bâtıl, bâtılı hak gösterme gayretlerini yansıtan, bütün küfür ve ilhad faaliyetlerini ifade eden bir terim olarak kullanılır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r2.speaker: Muhammed Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r2.claim: The author accepts Asad’s additional sense of tāghūt as the corrupting power of satanic passions that sever spiritual ties and enslave a person to emotion, without excluding other senses.
